analysis: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is primarily associated with deficiencies in Protein C and Protein S. When warfarin is initiated, it can lead to a rapid decrease in the levels of these proteins, which are crucial for regulating coagulation. In patients with Protein C deficiency, the risk of developing skin necrosis is significantly increased due to the lack of this anticoagulant protein, which normally helps to prevent clot formation in the microcirculation of the skin. Protein S deficiency also poses a risk, as it acts as a cofactor for Protein C. In contrast, Hemophilia and Antithrombin III deficiency do not have a direct association with warfarin-induced skin necrosis. Therefore, the most relevant options are Protein C deficiency and Protein S deficiency, with Protein C deficiency being the more established risk factor. Given this information, the best-supported option is Protein C deficiency.
